text:
alex: FYI — after the Docusaurus migration I noticed a bunch of broken fragment links coming from our product pages into /reference. Example that fails for me: https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/auth#token-refresh — it just bounces to the top of the page instead of the heading.

alex: Repro steps: 1) click link from product page TOC 2) lands on ref page 3) no scroll to section. Happens in Chrome and Firefox.

jamie: I saw that in staging previews too. Looks like slug generation changed (emoji and parens handling). Quick scan of the rendered HTML shows heading ids like "token-refresh-" vs the old "token-refresh".

sophia: Could be the new slugify behavior in docusaurus-plugin-content-docs. We changed versions during the migration. There are two options: add explicit header IDs in the markdown (e.g., `### Token refresh {#token-refresh}`) or normalize slugify settings in the config.

liam: Prefer a config-level fix if possible so we don't have to edit many files. Which setting controls that?

jamie: There's a `slugify` option and a `removeEmoji`/`lowercase` behavior. But we have a handful (~8) of hotspots where upstream content expects the old slugs. For those, explicit IDs are safest and minimal.

alex: I'm going to open a small patch to add explicit IDs for the affected headings and also add a note to the migration guide so this doesn't surprise folks. Will mark the PR with the list of pages.

jamie: Can you paste an example of the markdown change you plan to do?

alex: Sure — here's the pattern I used:```markdown
### Token refresh {#token-refresh}
Short paragraph about refresh flow.
```
This preserves the old anchor while letting docusaurus render normally.

sophia: That looks good. For the config path, I'll prototype `slugify: (s) => s.replace(/[\u200B-\u200F]/g, '').toLowerCase()` in my branch and run the full linkcheck. If that stabilizes all slugs we can roll it in and remove explicit IDs over time.

liam: OK, if we go config-first we should add a test in the linkcheck job so it fails CI if slugs diverge.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4293 opened. It updates 6 pages (reference/auth, reference/rate-limits, guides/migrations, examples/sdk-snippets). Includes a small script I used to diff old vs new slugs.

docs-ci-bot: Build preview started for PR 4293 — linkcheck step queued.

jamie: Thanks, alex. I left one nit (escape the inline `@client` example in the SDK snippet). Also added a test note to the PR description for docs reviewers.

docs-ci-bot: Linkcheck completed with 3 warnings and 0 hard failures. Two of the warnings are external redirect warnings.

alex: Merged PR 4293. Preview link: https://deploy-preview-4293--docs.redwood.ai/reference/auth — I tested the three fixed anchors and they jump properly now.

liam: Nice — can we add a short entry to the migration guide: 'Docusaurus slug changes may require explicit header ids for stable anchors'?

alex: Added a one-paragraph note in `docs/migration/docusaurus-2.2.md` in the same PR.

sophia: I'll continue with the config experiment in my branch and post results here. If it reduces churn we can follow up with a cleanup PR to remove explicit IDs.

jamie: Great work. :tada:

docs-ci-bot: Preview published: https://deploy-preview-4293--docs.redwood.ai/ — build id 2026-03-21-18:45

alex: Closing thread once we confirm internal links too. If anyone finds additional busted anchors please drop them here and I'll roll fixes into a small follow-up.

liam: Seen one more: `guides/auth#session-management` -> I'll raise an issue with the page path and old-vs-new slug diff.

alex: Thanks, noted.
